issues.detail: Main article is not available locally; coverage applies to the available SI preparation network only.
issues.subject: paper

issues.detail: Overview Scheme 1 annotates HCl; individual preparation drawing annotates HBr and elemental analysis uses C25H34BrN3O6. Covalent parent is stored separately; no isolated salt SMILES is asserted.
Drawings annotate HCl but procedures include aqueous bicarbonate workup and describe crude oils. Salt annotations are retained separately from source covalent graphs.
Source writes COCl2, but the two mass/mmol pairs imply approximately 127 g/mol. Reagent identity is unresolved; normalized SMILES remains null.
issues.subject: E01/E02

issues.detail: Comparison-table heading calls the natural/synthetic target 13 although Scheme 1 and preparation identify it as 1. Compound 13 in Scheme 2 is a distinct precursor.

Comparison table reports isolated-sample olefin J=12.5 Hz versus synthetic J=15.7 Hz, with olefin carbon differences 4.3 and 3.5 ppm. Preserve source-drawn synthetic E geometry; natural/synthetic identity is not independently established.
Procedure for 12 to 13 says compound 6 was consumed. Preparation heading and scheme identify 12; the conflicting text is retained as an issue.
issues.subject: E13

issues.detail: Quantitative yield remains qualitative; crude recovered masses are not converted into invented numeric isolated yields.
issues.subject: E03/E06/E11/E13

issues.detail: Two experimental stages are grouped per preparation; no source drawing exists for the internal acid chlorides or reduced amines.
issues.subject: E01/E02/E05/E10

issues.detail: Target is explicitly racemic; unassigned tetrahedral stereochemistry is retained, never completed to an arbitrary enantiomer.
Source writes LiOH; reported mass/mmol implies a hydrate. Normalization records named lithium hydroxide without asserting hydration.
issues.subject: E13
